subject: Batching & concurrency: long-tail throughput and $/1M token target - next steps
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Levin <sasha@neptuneanalytics.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-03T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Batch & concurrency: long-tail throughput and $/1M token target - next steps

Hi Sasha — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on economics and the PoC scope.

Recap (from our discovery):
- Primary workload: user-driven analytics queries with a long tail of complexity; median request ~120 tokens in, 280 tokens out; 95th ~1.2k tokens.
- Traffic pattern: steady baseline ~35 qps with periodic bursts to ~220 qps for ~15–45 minutes (trading hours).
- Expected monthly token volume: 20M–60M tokens in month 1; target growth to 200M+/mo over 6–9 months if latency & cost meet thresholds.
- Priority: predictable unit economics (target $/1M tokens) and consistent p95 latency <= 400ms for median requests.

Specific asks from us to finalize pricing/PoC:
1) Confirm a realistic budget band for initial 3-month PoC (range is fine). You mentioned procurement might aim for <$6k/month to start — can you confirm if that is firm or flexible?
2) Agree on target $/1M tokens for us to size dedicated vs hosted options. If you have a target (e.g., $X / 1M tokens) state it; we can map pricing tiers to that.
3) Provide a small sample of timestamped traffic (CSV) with token counts and concurrency windows so our infra team can run a continuous-batching profile — I attached our sample template.

What Redwood proposes (high level):
- Pilot plan: 4-week technical PoC + 8-week performance/econ observation period.
- Instrumentation: we’ll run continuous batching enabled on a hosted dedicated pool and share token-level cost breakdown.
- Pricing: provisional bands in attached XLSX — they are placeholders until we get confirmed volumes and concurrency shape.

Next steps / timeline:
- Sasha: send the sample CSV + procurement guidance (budget range) by EOD Thu (8/6).
- Redwood (Ben/Rishi): run a continuous-batching throughput simulation and return a runbook + provisional pricing by Mon (8/10).

Attachments: workload sample template (neptune_workload_samples_v2.csv), provisional pricing workbook (redwood_provisional_pricing_DN-4582.xlsx).

Thanks — happy to jump on a short follow-up if helpful.

—
Avery Johnson

Thanks, Avery — great summary. A few quick notes and answers inline: 

Budget: procurement is targeting an initial window of $4k–$8k/month for tooling/pilot, with flexibility for a short-term overage if the PoC demonstrates clear value. They asked for a clear ROI slide for any ask above $8k.

$/1M token target: Our finance lead suggested we aim for <= $300 per 1M tokens for the hosted option during the PoC. Long term, we'd like to see the number closer to $120–$150 per 1M for production at scale (200M+).

Traffic samples: attaching a trimmed export with timestamp, tokens_in, tokens_out, and request_id. Note the heavy-tail events cluster during market open hours (09:30–10:15 ET).

Operational notes: low tolerance for noisy tail latency during trading windows. If continuous batching adds jitter above p95 targets we will need fallback rules.

I attached the CSV (neptune_workload_samples_v2.csv). Procurement looped in for contract terms.

Sasha / Avery — thanks for the sample, Sasha. I ran an initial continuous-batching profile against the CSV and a few quick takeaways:

Quick profile (summary):
- Median request tokens (in+out): ~400 tokens; mean ~540 tokens; 95th ~1.4k tokens.
- Effective batching window tolerated: 5–18ms for median flows; during burst windows we see batching windows up to ~60ms without hurting median p95 by more than ~20–30ms.
- Continuous batching reduces per-token compute by ~22–29% for this long-tail shape versus naive immediate-exec.

Econ sketch (provisional):
- For the PoC volumes (20M–60M tokens/month): estimated hosted unit cost range $240–$360 per 1M tokens (includes model compute, network, and amortized infra for observed concurrency). This maps to $4.8k–$21.6k/month depending on where in that volume band you land.
- For steady-state at scale (200M+/mo) with aggressive batching + quantization profiles: we can get closer to your target $120–$160 per 1M tokens on dedicated capacity.

Notes and risks:
- Tail events during market open increase amortized cost per token because they push higher concurrency and reduce batching efficiency for those minutes. If those windows are predictable we can offer a hybrid routing policy (burst capacity) to keep unit economics stable.
- If p95 latency for median requests must be <=400ms strict, we recommend configuring a p95 SLO-based routing policy (route median to lower-cost pooled variants, fall back to smaller-batch low-latency nodes during spikes).

I’ve attached a provisional pricing workbook with scenarios mapped to volume bands and routing/batching configs. It includes a candidate deal structure for DN-4582.

Next step — Avery / Sasha: can you confirm which volume assumption we should price first (20M or 60M)? Also would procurement prefer a capped-monthly-commit vs usage-plus-overage pricing for the PoC?

—
Ben Carter
